body.summary: The spring nine nights of the Goddess, Shailaputri to Siddhidatri, closing as Rama Navami.

why.text: The Devi Kavacha names the nine Durgas, spoken by Brahma himself.
The first three days are Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, and Chandraghanta.
The middle three days are Kushmanda, Skandamata, and Katyayani.
The last three days are Kalaratri, Mahagauri, and Siddhidatri.
The Devi Mahatmya sings of the Goddess felling the buffalo demon Mahisha, remembered on Vijayadashami.

gather.text: A kalash, water, mango leaves, and a coconut for ghatasthapana.
Clean soil and barley seeds to sow beside the kalash.
A photo or murti of Durga and a red cloth for the seat.
Red flowers, akshat, roli, and kumkum for the daily puja.
A ghee or oil diya, incense, and a bell.
The Durga Saptashati, Durga Chalisa, or Devi Kavacha for reading.
Fruits, halwa, poori, and kheer for bhog offerings.
For kanya pujan: bangles, bindis, mauli thread, and small gifts.

steps.text: On day one, spread clean soil and sow barley seeds beside the kalash, invoking the Goddess (ghatasthapana).
Set the kalash with water, leaves, and coconut, place the murti, and light a diya for the nine days.
Read or chant the Devi Kavacha, Durga Saptashati, or Durga Chalisa daily.
Offer water, red flowers, akshat, and fresh bhog to the Goddess each morning.
Sit before the kalash morning and evening, and repeat the Durga mantra or her names.
Worship the nine forms one by one, a new form for each day of the series.
On Ashtami, offer bhog during the sandhi puja window at the junction of the two tithis.
On Ashtami or Navami, welcome young girls for kanya pujan: wash their feet and tie the mauli.
Serve them puri, halwa, and chana, and give bangles and a small gift with respect.
On Dashami, close with a final puja, and immerse or keep the barley plants and kalash as your family follows.

budget.text: Reuse a clean cloth and the deity's picture already at home.
Set aside water and a small seasonal offering from what you have.
Keep the observance simple: prayer and attention, with any lamp placed safely.

eat.text: Many take one sattvic meal a day, after the evening puja.
Fruits, milk, curd, makhana, and nuts are the usual day food.
Sabudana, kuttu, singhare, and rajgira dishes for a grain-free fast.
Use rock salt (sendha namak) in place of common salt while fasting.

avoid.text: Alcohol and all intoxicants are set aside for the nine days.
Meat, fish, and eggs are avoided in most houses.
Onion and garlic stay out of the kitchen.
Lentils, common salt, and regular grains are left out while fasting.

break.text: The fast closes with kanya pujan or the Navami puja, before Dashami.
Some families break on Ashtami after the sandhi puja; follow your family's practice.

who_should_eat.text: Children, the elderly, the ill, and pregnant women are free from fasting.
Anyone on medical advice should eat normally and ask their doctor.
A partial fast with one simple meal suits those who cannot fast fully.

types.text: Phalahar: fruit and foods accepted in your family's vrat tradition.
One-meal observance: a simple meal rather than a complete fast.
Selected-day observance: some families keep the first and last days instead of all nine.

dont.text: Most families avoid haircuts, shaving, and nail cutting through the nine days.
Stitching and cutting cloth are avoided during the festival.
Keep leather items like belts and wallets away from the puja area.
Avoid anger, lies, and harsh speech; the days are kept calm and sattvic.
Do not let the akhand jyoti go out; keep the diya lit through the nine nights.

texts.title: Narayani Stuti (the Durga mantra)
texts.devanagari: सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके। शरण्ये त्र्यम्बके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते॥
texts.iast: sarva-maṅgala-māṅgalye śive sarvārtha-sādhike | śaraṇye tryambake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te ||
texts.meaning: O auspicious one, the blessing of every blessing, Shiva's consort who fulfils every aim, my refuge, three-eyed Gauri: Narayani, I bow to you.

texts.title: The nine Durgas (Devi Kavacha)
texts.devanagari: प्रथमं शैलपुत्री च द्वितीयं ब्रह्मचारिणी। तृतीयं चन्द्रघण्टेति कूष्माण्डेति चतुर्थकम्॥ पञ्चमं स्कन्दमातेति षष्ठं कात्यायनीति च। सप्तमं कालरात्रिति महागौरीति चाष्टमम्॥ नवमं सिद्धिदात्री च नवदुर्गाः प्रकीर्तिताः। उक्तान्येतानि नामानि ब्रह्मणैव महात्मना॥
texts.iast: prathamaṃ śailaputrī ca dvitīyaṃ brahmacāriṇī | tṛtīyaṃ candraghaṇṭeti kūṣmāṇḍeti caturthakam || pañcamaṃ skandamāteti ṣaṣṭhaṃ kātyāyanīti ca | saptamaṃ kālarātriti mahāgaurīti cāṣṭamam || navamaṃ siddhidātrī ca navadurgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ | uktāny etāni nāmāni brahmaṇaiva mahātmanā ||
texts.meaning: First Shailaputri, second Brahmacharini, third Chandraghanta, fourth Kushmanda, fifth Skandamata, sixth Katyayani, seventh Kalaratri, eighth Mahagauri, ninth Siddhidatri: these nine Durgas are celebrated, names spoken by Brahma himself.

texts.title: Ambe Gauri aarti (opening)
texts.devanagari: जय अम्बे गौरी, मैया जय श्यामा गौरी॥ तुमको निशदिन ध्यावत, हरि ब्रह्मा शिवरी॥
texts.iast: jai ambe gaurī maiyā jai śyāmā gaurī || tumako niśadin dhyāvata hari brahmā śivarī ||
texts.meaning: Victory to Mother Gauri, the dark and the fair: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva worship you day and night. Sung at the aarti through Navaratri.

series_days.summary: Daughter of the mountain, who rides the bull bearing a trident and lotus, crowned with the crescent moon; the first form of the nine.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Shailaputri at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the mountain's daughter whose trident opens the nine nights.

texts.title: Shailaputri dhyana
texts.devanagari: वन्दे वाञ्छितलाभाय चन्द्रार्धकृतशेखराम्। वृषारूढां शूलधरां शैलपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम्॥
texts.iast: vande vāñchitalābhāya candrārdhakṛtaśekharām | vṛṣārūḍhāṃ śūladharāṃ śailaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm ||
texts.meaning: I bow to fortunate Shailaputri, crowned with the crescent moon, mounted on the bull, bearing a trident, who grants desired boons.

series_days.summary: The maiden of penance, walking barefoot with a rosary and water pot; her tapas carries the second day.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Brahmacharini at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the serene student who pursues the highest aim.

texts.title: Brahmacharini dhyana
texts.devanagari: दधाना करपद्माभ्यामक्षमालाकमण्डलू। देवी प्रसीदतु मयि ब्रह्मचारिण्यनुत्तमा॥
texts.iast: dadānā karapadmābhyām akṣamālā kamaṇḍalū | devī prasīdatu mayi brahmacāriṇy anuttamā ||
texts.meaning: Holding a rosary and a water pot in her lotus hands, may the supreme Brahmacharini be gracious to me.

series_days.summary: The bell-moon at her brow, riding the lion, serene yet armed; her bell is said to still every fear.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Chandraghanta at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the armed one whose grace is asked before any new work.

texts.title: Chandraghanta dhyana
texts.devanagari: पिण्डजप्रवरारूढा चण्डकोपास्त्रकैर्युता। प्रसादं तनुते मह्यां चन्द्रघण्टेति विश्रुता॥
texts.iast: piṇḍajapravarārūḍhā caṇḍakopāstrakairyutā | prasādaṃ tanute mahyāṃ candraghaṇṭeti viśrutā ||
texts.meaning: Mounted on the best of lions, fierce with her weapons in wrath, the famed Chandraghanta bestows her grace on me.

series_days.summary: She who dwells inside the sun's orb, whose smile kindled the cosmic egg; her laughter begins creation.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Kushmanda at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the warmth at the heart of the sun who gives all good.

texts.title: Kushmanda dhyana
texts.devanagari: सुरासम्पूर्णकलशं रुधिराप्लुतमेव च। दधाना हस्तपद्माभ्यां कूष्माण्डा शुभदास्तु मे॥
texts.iast: surāsampūrṇakalaśaṃ rudhirāplutameva ca | dadānā hastapadmābhyāṃ kūṣmāṇḍā śubhadāstu me ||
texts.meaning: Holding a brimming chalice and lotuses in her hands, may Kushmanda grant me good.

series_days.summary: Mother of Skanda, seated on the lotus throne with the child Kumara on her lap; she is prayed to as a mother first.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Skandamata at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the mother whose lap carries the boy commander of the gods.

texts.title: Skandamata dhyana
texts.devanagari: सिंहासनगता नित्यं पद्माश्रितकरद्वया। शुभदास्तु सदा देवी स्कन्दमाता यशस्विनी॥
texts.iast: siṃhāsanagatā nityaṃ padmāśritakaradvayā | śubhadāstu sadā devī skandamātā yaśasvinī ||
texts.meaning: Seated ever on the lion throne, her two hands resting on lotuses, may the fortunate Skandamata ever give me good.

series_days.summary: Daughter of the sage Katyayana, radiant as the moon's smile, riding the noble lion; the form young women pray to for a good match.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Katyayani at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the slayer of demons who gives good to her devotees.

texts.title: Katyayani dhyana
texts.devanagari: चन्द्रहासोज्ज्वलकरा शार्दूलवरवाहना। कात्यायनी शुभं दद्याद्देवी दानवघातिनी॥
texts.iast: candrahāsojjvalakarā śārdūlavaravāhanā | kātyāyanī śubhaṃ dadyād devī dānavaghātinī ||
texts.meaning: Her hand radiant with the moon's smile, riding the noble lion: may Katyayani, the slayer of demons, give me good.

series_days.summary: The dark night form, fierce yet blessing, mounted on the donkey; she is remembered as the burner of fear itself.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Kalaratri at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the terrifying one who is still a mother to her devotees.

texts.title: Kalaratri dhyana
texts.devanagari: एकवेणी जपाकर्णपूरा नग्ना खरास्थिता। लम्बोष्ठी कर्णिकाकर्णी तैलाभ्यक्तशरीरिणी॥ वामपादोल्लसल्लोहलताकण्टकभूषणा। वर्धनमूर्धध्वजा कृष्णा कालरात्रिर्भयङ्करी॥
texts.iast: ekaveṇī japākarṇapūrā nagnā kharāsthitā | lamboṣṭhī karṇikākarṇī tailābhyaktaśarīriṇī || vāmapādollasallohalatākaṇṭakabhūṣaṇā | vardhanamūrdhadhvajā kṛṣṇā kālarātrir bhayaṅkarī ||
texts.meaning: Single-braided, japa flowers at her ears, standing on the donkey, long-lipped, anointed with oil, adorned with iron and thorns, her banner raised: the dark Kalaratri, awesome to behold.

series_days.summary: The fair one on the white bull, robed in white and washed pure; calm, four-armed, and delighting Mahadeva.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Mahagauri at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the pure one whose forgiveness is asked of every fault.

texts.title: Mahagauri dhyana
texts.devanagari: श्वेते वृषे समारूढा श्वेताम्बरधरा शुचिः। महागौरी शुभं दघान्महादेवप्रमोददा॥
texts.iast: śvete vṛṣe samārūḍhā śvetāmbaradharā śuciḥ | mahāgaurī śubhaṃ daghān mahādevapramodadā ||
texts.meaning: Mounted on the white bull, robed in white, pure: may Mahagauri, the delight of Mahadeva, give me good.

series_days.summary: The giver of siddhis, seated on the lotus and served by siddhas, gandharvas, and gods; she crowns the nine nights.

steps.text: Offer fresh flowers and the day's bhog to Siddhidatri at the kalash.
Read or sing her salutation verse from the Nava Durga Stotram.
Remember her as the fulfilment who grants every attainment to the devoted.

texts.title: Siddhidatri dhyana
texts.devanagari: सिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षाघैरसुरैरमरैरपि। सेव्यमाना सदा भूयात् सिद्धिदा सिद्धिदायिनी॥
texts.iast: siddhagandharvayakṣādyair asurair amarair api | seviamānā sadā bhūyāt siddhidā siddhidāyinī ||
texts.meaning: Served by siddhas, gandharvas, yakshas, asuras, and immortals: may Siddhida, the giver of attainments, ever be near.

sources.text_name: Navratri fasting rules and pooja vidhi
